title: Area2D body_exited signal called mid program quit if connected to node lower in scene tree, causing crashes if receiving node tries to access the scene tree
body:
### Tested versions

Reproduced in v4.6.3.stable.official [7d41c59c4], v4.7.beta5.official [bbd3f43b5]

### System information

Windows 10 (build 19045) - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop GPU (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9227) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-13700HX (24 threads) - 31.70 GiB memory

### Issue description

Area2D nodes will emit the body_exited signal before being removed from the scene tree after SceneTree.quit() is called if and only if:
- There is a physics body inside the area and _higher_ in the scene tree
- The signal is connected to a node _lower_ in the scene tree

This causes a crash if the receiving node attempts to access the scene tree, as it has already been removed from the tree. In my game where I encountered this, this was due to a child of an Area2D trying to access the camera through get_viewport().get_camera_2d(), but it happens with any use of get_tree() or get_viewport().

Sufficient code for recreating this (with the scene tree set up appropriately):
```gdscript
extends Area2D

func _input(event: InputEvent) -> void:
	if event.is_action_pressed("ui_accept"):
		get_tree().quit()

func _ready() -> void:
	body_exited.connect(on_body_exited)
	
	body_exited.connect($Node2D.test)

func on_body_exited(body: Node2D) -> void:
	print("exited")
	assert(get_tree() != null)
```
```gdscript
extends Node2D

func test(_body: Node2D) -> void:
	assert(get_tree() != null)
```

Digging around I found this very old issue which refers to the callback occurring during quit as "desirable": https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/53563  Personally I cannot see where this would ever be the case - I would fully expect all physics callbacks to stop entirely once the program begins to quit. Even if the signal occurring in some form _is_ desired for whatever reason, the current behavior being so heavily dependent on scene tree ordering makes it extremely unpredictable and error prone and seems clearly buggy.

### Steps to reproduce

Run the MRP and press enter to quit the game. The game should freeze and throw an assertion error from test() in child.gd, which is only ever ran through the body_exited signal.

Note that:
- Commenting out the connection to the child node will cause the "exited" print statement to never run, as will changing the connection to a node higher in the tree, implying the body_exited callback does not occur at all without a node lower in the tree connected to it
- The error still occurs if the child node is moved to be a sibling of the area instead, as long as it is lower in the scene tree
- The error stops occurring if the physics body is moved below the area in the tree

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[bug-test-(4.6).zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28651981/bug-test-.4.6.zip)
